- We rolled v23b to 100% traffic in us-west-2 at 07:50 PDT as part of the scheduled rollout.
- Early traces show an increase in KV-cache misses under certain prompt prefixes and a CPU hot path at the attention kernel for longer sequences.
- The runtime is throttling some requests which is producing tail amplification under high concurrency.

Sofia — quick recommendation after reviewing the profiling snapshot:

1) Controlled fencing + weighted diversion (recommended):
   - Move 60% of ClearBank's traffic to v23a via routing policy for the next 2 hours.
   - Keep 40% on v23b to collect production signals and confirm whether tail behavior stabilizes after heat dissipation / cache warm.
   - This avoids a full rollback and limits risk of rollforward instability.

2) Conditional rollback (escalated option):
   - Authorize a 30-minute emergency rollback window to v23a if p95 does not return to <1.5s within 45 minutes.
   - Legal/Finance must sign an SLA carveout addendum for any credits tied to rollback-driven service changes (see downtime-credit-terms.pdf).

Tradeoffs: fencing reduces risk but may obscure a persistent regression metric; rollback restores baseline but has delivery risk for other edge workloads because of stateful config differences in v23a.

I propose we ask the customer which path they prefer, and request kim to approve the conditional rollback threshold and credit terms.

-Ben
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Clara — summarizing the action plan we executed and next steps. Thank you for the patience while we stabilized traffic.

What we did (timeline):
- 10:10 PDT: Activated weighted diversion (60% v23a, 40% v23b) for ClearBank via routing policy. No client-visible downtime.
- 10:25 PDT: Observed p95 reduce from ~6.4s to 1.3s for the diverted traffic; remaining v23b bucket showed transient oscillation with a slow recovery.
- 10:55 PDT: Continued decrease in tail events; after 45 minutes post-diversion p95 for entire account settled to 1.2s (within your SLA threshold).

Agreed conditional path:
- If p95 had remained above 1.5s after 45 minutes, we were prepared to execute a 30-minute rollback to v23a. Kimberly authorized this conditional rollback and legal prepared credit terms in case rollback was used.

Outcome and next steps:
- We did NOT perform a full rollback because the weighted diversion stabilized your traffic and preserved observability for the remaining v23b subset.
- We attached the profiling snapshot (v23b-profiling-snapshot.zip) and a short post-incident note; engineering will open INF-4721 for follow-up mitigation (kernel patch and cache policy tuning).
- As a courtesy, Redwood will issue a technical incident summary and a one-time service credit offer conditional on contract terms (see downtime-credit-terms.pdf). Clara, if you accept the credit offer, I'll loop in Legal and Billing to finalize paperwork.

Please let me know if you want us to 1) schedule a deeper post-mortem with your SREs next week, or 2) trigger a temporary pin on your side for additional safety during our next canary rollout.

Thanks again — we aim to prevent reoccurrence and will prioritize the kernel optimization in INF-4721.

Sofia Ivanova
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
